probe: artifacts/askq-probe-tools/codex-appserver-probe.js (ignored local tool): a hidden codex app-server on a loopback websocket with a capability token, isolated CODEX_HOME and a loopback fixture model; a client starts one thread and one turn whose model calls request_user_input, never answers, and polls thread/read for about 12 s. No person involved.
findings: The owning runtime exposes a user-input wait signal: thread/status becomes active with activeFlags [waitingOnUserInput] when the question dialog is raised, thread/read keeps returning it while the dialog is unanswered, and the server sends item/tool/requestUserInput to the client. It is the question analogue of waitingOnApproval.
The signal appears in Plan mode and in Default mode with the experimental feature, within about 20 ms of the tool call.
No waitingOnApproval flag appeared in either scenario: in the Codex runtime the question dialog is not an approval request (unlike Claude, where it runs through the approval flow).
Default mode without the feature rejects the call before any dialog (pre-apply capture), so no flag is expected there.
